question: What does gov.uk say about the personal allowance for 2026-27 in England?
report:
For 2026-27 in England, GOV.UK gives the standard Personal Allowance as £12,570.00 (https://www.gov.uk/income-tax-rates).

Supporting GOV.UK pages:

- **Income Tax rates and Personal Allowances** (https://www.gov.uk/income-tax-rates): sets out the tax rates and bands table, which assumes the standard Personal Allowance, and notes that Income Tax bands are different if you live in Scotland.
- **Rates and thresholds for employers 2026 to 2027** (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/rates-and-thresholds-for-employers-2026-to-2027): covers the tax codes and thresholds used when deducting Income Tax through payroll.

Since your profile is set as a non-Scottish taxpayer, the England, Wales and Northern Ireland rates apply.

If it would help, I can look up the basic, higher and additional rate thresholds, or the allowance taper threshold, as separate rule lookups.
